tests.description: A handler function writes a global while answering an interrupt from its own branch. The write is kept.

A handler function writes a global while answering interrupts from fork branches. The writes go to the raising branch's copy of the globals, and that copy is dropped when the branch ends, so the parent's global is unchanged. This is the branch isolation the guide describes under state isolation: the handler function runs where the interrupt was raised.

A handler function writes a global while answering two interrupts: the one for starting a subprocess, raised in its own branch, and one raised inside the subprocess. The first write is kept. The second goes to the subprocess call's own copy of the globals, for the same reason as in forkBranch.
